summary: commonjs-assert typosquat fetches and evaluates remote JavaScript on require
details: Package impersonates a chai/assert-style assertion library (name 'commonjs-assert', chai-derived description and keywords, homepage commonjs-assert.com, re-exports chai from./lib/chai). On require, index.js hex-decodes the strings 'child_process' and 'spawn' and detach-spawns `node./lib/chai/utils/assertion.js` with stdio ignored. That file is heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation and a custom base64 decoder, uses https.get to fetch a remote body, and passes the response to `new Function('require', body)(require)`, executing attacker-controlled JavaScript with full Node privileges. The obfuscation hides the module identifiers ('https', hostname, 'data'/'end', 'utf8'/'base64', 'atob') and the destination URL used for the fetch-and-eval flow.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
